extra.reason: Implemented diatom-side: new state-plane protocol verbs SPEED/SETSPEED (frame-pacing multiplier, 1..8x) and REWIND/SETREWIND (ring-buffer step-back), diatom/src/rewind.c (new ring buffer module), diatom ADR-0034 documenting the design and settling the scoping register's [LB] rewind-RAM item. Full detail and verification in diatom commit 03c92fc on branch feature/1v7.3-ff-rewind (diatom repo, local, not pushed). TortOS/launcher side needs NO new code: the existing generic plat_resident_line() (src/platform.h) already sends any one protocol line to Diatom, so a caller (the hotkey submenu, bead .2) can invoke SETSPEED/SETREWIND directly once it exists -- confirmed by reading platform.h's own doc comment before writing a redundant wrapper. TortOS-side feature/1v7.3-ff-rewind branch has zero commits, correctly, since nothing needed changing there. VERIFICATION CEILING (stated precisely, not glossed): this environment has no SDL2 installed and no privilege to install it, so diatom's own /conform-check/check-proto/check-stateplane could not run (they need to link and run the real SDL-backed binary against a stub core). What WAS verified: (1) the entire non-port source tree compiles clean, zero warnings; (2) a standalone SDL-free harness drives the real proto.c parser over a live Unix socket, confirming SETSPEED/SPEED/SETREWIND/REWIND all decode correctly plus a regression check that SETMUTE still parses; (3) a standalone SDL-free harness drives rewind.c's real ring-buffer code against a fake diatom_core covering capture/restore roundtrip, ring wraparound (12 captures into an 8-slot ring preserves exactly the newest 8), mid-session serialize_size growth (reproducing the exact scenario save.c's own comment measured on mGBA), ring exhaustion, and a core with no savestate support -- all 20 assertions pass; (4) diatom's own make check-seam/check-register/check-corefacts/check-rates still pass (worked around this environment's missing-SDL2 Makefile guard via a command-line variable override for these SDL-free targets only, not a code change). NOT verified: actual gameplay with a real core/ROM (frame pacing math and the FF-quiets-audio interaction are code-reviewed, not executed against a running session), and the 8MB rewind memory budget is an explicit placeholder pending real per-core serialize_size() measurement on the actual Brick hardware (ADR-0034's Revisit-if).
